verdict.rationale: LightSprint documents a plan-first workflow for larger features, where the team picks options and mockups before anything is built and then hands the plan off as an implementation task. That approximates aligning on scope before the agent writes code. The other review and approval controls (diff summaries, screenshots, Review Hub, merge authority) all act after the change is built, so they do not count as a pre-modification gate. Missing for 10: an explicit approval gate that blocks the agent from touching the repo until signed off, a formal scope or contract artifact, an engineering-lead approval role for plans, applicability beyond 'larger features', and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can approve a task's scope and contract before an agent is allowed to modify the repository

citations.quote: For larger features, plan first and align as a team. Pick options and mockups before anything is built, then hand the plan off as one implementation task.
